newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomb judge denies defense request.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomb judge denies defense request.

text.p: The judge in the Oklahoma City bombing trial denied on Wednesday a defence request for a pre-trial hearing to decide if results of certain FBI lab testing should be admitted at next month's trial.
U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch said in a written order that a hearing was not necessary and that the defence could raise any objections at the trial.
A hearing on the matter outside the presence of the jury could be held at that time, the judge said.

The results in question involve testing for chemical residue on the clothing and personal property taken from defendant Timothy McVeigh and on analytical testing on an unidentified object taken from the explosion site.

The defence had wanted a pre-trial hearing to examine the qualifications of three witnesses. The attorneys argued that there was a possibility the items tested were contaminated at the lab, that FBI lab procedures were improper and that unqualified people participated in the tests.
The judge said the prosecution at the trial would have to establish that proper testing methods were used and the persons testifying were qualified.
"All of the necessary foundation must be proved ... before questions asking for opinions and conclusions will be permitted," the judge wrote.
McVeigh's attorney Stephen Jones told reporters: "He (Matsch) simply has delayed it until the time of the trial which is entirely satisfactory to us."
"There are some strategic advantages for us in doing it that way," Jones added.

An inspector general report on the Federal Bureau of Investigation crime laboratory, not yet publicly released, has criticised the FBI lab for poor management practices and sloppy handling of evidence.
"We're ecstatic about the judge's ruling that we won't have any pre-trial hearing on our experts," prosecutor Beth Wilkinson said.

Jones told reporters after a closed-door scheduling conference that a pre-trial hearing on defence challenges to records of telephone calls allegedly made by McVeigh in the months before the bombing was cancelled and that the matter will be taken up at the trial.

McVeigh and his former army buddy Terry Nichols are charged in the April 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building that claimed the lives of 168 people. McVeigh's trial starts on March 31 and Nichols will be tried later at an undetermined date.
